chapters.title: The call of Jeremiah
chapters.summary: God calls young Jeremiah: before I formed you in the womb I knew you. He touches his mouth and gives visions of an almond branch and a boiling pot.

chapters.title: Broken cisterns
chapters.summary: God remembers Israel's early devotion, but now they have forsaken Him, the fountain of living waters, and dug broken cisterns.

chapters.title: Return, faithless Israel
chapters.summary: Judah has seen Israel's unfaithfulness and done worse. Still God calls: return, and I will give you shepherds after My own heart.

chapters.title: Disaster from the north
chapters.summary: God calls for true repentance, a circumcised heart, and warns of an invader from the north. Jeremiah is anguished at the coming ruin.

chapters.title: Not one honest person
chapters.summary: God searches Jerusalem for one person who acts justly and finds none. The people have stubborn hearts, and the prophets prophesy falsely.

chapters.title: Ask for the old paths
chapters.summary: Jerusalem is besieged in vision. Prophets say "peace, peace" when there is no peace. Stand at the crossroads and ask for the ancient paths.

chapters.title: The temple sermon
chapters.summary: At the temple gate Jeremiah warns that trusting the temple will not save people who steal, murder and worship other gods. Has this house become a den of robbers?

chapters.title: Is there no balm in Gilead?
chapters.summary: The people do not repent, and their wise men have rejected God's word. Jeremiah grieves: is there no balm in Gilead?

chapters.title: Let him who boasts
chapters.summary: Jeremiah weeps for his people. Let no one boast in wisdom, strength or riches, but in knowing the Lord who exercises lovingkindness and justice.

chapters.title: The living God and the idols
chapters.summary: Idols are like scarecrows in a field, but the Lord is the true and living God. Jeremiah prays for correction with justice.

chapters.title: The broken covenant
chapters.summary: Judah has broken the covenant. Men of Anathoth, Jeremiah's own town, plot to kill him like a lamb led to the slaughter.

chapters.title: Why do the wicked prosper?
chapters.summary: Jeremiah asks why the wicked prosper. God answers that harder trials are coming: if you have run with footmen and they wearied you, how will you race with horses?

chapters.title: The ruined belt
chapters.summary: Jeremiah buries a linen belt until it rots, a picture of Judah's pride ruined. Can a leopard change its spots?

chapters.title: Drought and false prophets
chapters.summary: In a severe drought, Jeremiah pleads for the people, but God says not to pray for them, and condemns prophets who promise peace.

chapters.title: Jeremiah's complaint
chapters.summary: Even Moses and Samuel could not turn God's judgment. Jeremiah laments his birth, and God promises to make him a wall of bronze.

chapters.title: Signs of coming exile
chapters.summary: Jeremiah is told not to marry or attend feasts, as signs of coming disaster. But God will one day bring Israel back.

chapters.title: The heart is deceitful
chapters.summary: Cursed is the one who trusts in man; blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord, like a tree planted by water. The heart is deceitful above all things. Keep the Sabbath.

chapters.title: The potter's house
chapters.summary: Jeremiah watches a potter reshape a spoiled pot: as clay in the potter's hand, so are you in Mine. The people plot against him.

chapters.title: The broken jar
chapters.summary: Jeremiah smashes a clay jar before the elders as a sign that God will break Jerusalem for its idolatry and child sacrifice.

chapters.title: Fire in my bones
chapters.summary: Pashhur the priest beats Jeremiah and puts him in stocks. Jeremiah feels deceived, yet God's word is like a fire shut up in his bones.

chapters.title: The way of life and death
chapters.summary: King Zedekiah asks Jeremiah for help as Babylon attacks. God sets before them the way of life and the way of death: surrender to Babylon to live.

chapters.title: Warnings to the kings
chapters.summary: The kings of Judah must do justice and protect the poor. Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin are judged.

chapters.title: The righteous Branch
chapters.summary: Woe to the shepherds who scatter God's flock. God will raise for David a righteous Branch, the Lord our righteousness, and condemns lying prophets.

chapters.title: Two baskets of figs
chapters.summary: Good figs stand for the exiles God will bring back and give a heart to know Him; bad figs for those who stay in rebellion.

chapters.title: Seventy years
chapters.summary: After twenty-three years of warnings, Jeremiah announces seventy years of servitude to Babylon and the cup of God's wrath for all nations.

chapters.title: Jeremiah on trial
chapters.summary: Jeremiah's temple sermon brings a death sentence, but some elders recall Micah's prophecy and he is spared.

chapters.title: The yoke of Babylon
chapters.summary: Jeremiah wears a wooden yoke and tells the kings to submit to Nebuchadnezzar, and not listen to prophets who say otherwise.

chapters.title: Hananiah's false prophecy
chapters.summary: The prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's yoke and promises a quick return. Jeremiah says an iron yoke will replace it, and Hananiah dies that year.

chapters.title: Letter to the exiles
chapters.summary: Jeremiah writes to the exiles: build houses, seek the peace of the city, for I know the plans I have for you, plans for peace and a future and a hope.

chapters.title: Restoration promised
chapters.summary: Jeremiah is told to write down God's promise: a time of trouble for Jacob, but He will heal their wounds and bring them home.

chapters.title: The new covenant
chapters.summary: God has loved Israel with an everlasting love. He promises a new covenant: I will put My law in their hearts and remember their sin no more.

chapters.title: Jeremiah buys a field
chapters.summary: During the siege, Jeremiah buys a field as a sign that land will again be bought in Judah. Ah Lord God, nothing is too hard for You.

chapters.title: Call to me
chapters.summary: Call to Me and I will answer and show you great and hidden things. God promises healing and a righteous Branch from David.

chapters.title: Broken promise of freedom
chapters.summary: The people free their Hebrew slaves during the siege, then take them back. God proclaims freedom to sword and famine instead.

chapters.title: The faithful Rechabites
chapters.summary: The Rechabites refuse wine out of obedience to their ancestor, a rebuke to Judah who will not obey God.

chapters.title: The king burns the scroll
chapters.summary: Baruch writes Jeremiah's words on a scroll and reads it. King Jehoiakim cuts it up and burns it, and God has the scroll written again.

chapters.title: Jeremiah imprisoned
chapters.summary: Accused of deserting to Babylon, Jeremiah is beaten and imprisoned. Zedekiah secretly asks him for a word from the Lord.

chapters.title: The cistern
chapters.summary: Officials throw Jeremiah into a muddy cistern. Ebed-melech the Ethiopian rescues him, and Jeremiah urges Zedekiah to surrender.

chapters.title: Jerusalem falls
chapters.summary: Babylon breaks into Jerusalem. Zedekiah is captured and blinded, the city burned, and Jeremiah is released. Ebed-melech is promised safety.

chapters.title: Gedaliah governor
chapters.summary: Jeremiah chooses to stay in Judah with Gedaliah, the new governor, who urges the people to settle and serve Babylon.

chapters.title: Gedaliah murdered
chapters.summary: Ishmael murders Gedaliah and many others. Johanan rescues the captives, and the survivors fear Babylon's revenge.

chapters.title: Do not go to Egypt
chapters.summary: The survivors ask Jeremiah to pray for guidance and promise to obey. God says to stay in Judah and not flee to Egypt.

chapters.title: Taken to Egypt
chapters.summary: The leaders call Jeremiah a liar and take everyone, including Jeremiah, to Egypt. He foretells Nebuchadnezzar's invasion there.

chapters.title: The queen of heaven
chapters.summary: In Egypt the people insist on burning incense to the queen of heaven. Jeremiah announces judgment on them.

chapters.title: A word to Baruch
chapters.summary: Jeremiah's scribe Baruch is weary and sorrowful. God tells him not to seek great things for himself, but promises to spare his life.

chapters.title: Egypt
chapters.summary: The oracles against the nations begin with Egypt's defeat by Babylon at Carchemish, while Israel is told not to fear.

chapters.title: The Philistines
chapters.summary: The sword of the Lord will come against the Philistine cities.

chapters.title: Moab
chapters.summary: Proud Moab, which trusted in its works and treasures, will be broken, though God will restore it in the latter days.

chapters.title: Ammon, Edom, Damascus and Elam
chapters.summary: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Hazor and Elam, with promises of restoration for some.

chapters.title: Babylon will fall
chapters.summary: Babylon, God's instrument of judgment, will itself be destroyed. Israel and Judah will return weeping and seek the Lord.

chapters.title: God's judgment on Babylon
chapters.summary: Babylon was a golden cup in God's hand; now she will fall suddenly. Jeremiah's scroll is sunk in the Euphrates.

chapters.title: The fall of Jerusalem
chapters.summary: A historical account of Jerusalem's capture, the temple's destruction and the exile. In Babylon, King Jehoiachin is later released and treated kindly.
